items.q: Strategic drift occurs when a business:
opts: Implements a plan to cope with unexpected changes
Introduces an unplanned strategy in response to external changes
Introduces an unplanned strategy in response to internal changes
Maintains a strategy no longer suited to current circumstances
items.why: Strategic drift = continuing with a strategy that is no longer appropriate because the business environment has changed. The business has failed to adapt. A describes contingency planning. B describes emergent strategy. Drift = failing to change. The business drifts away from what the market needs because it keeps doing the same thing.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Nexon Consumer Goods sells three distinct product ranges — kitchen appliances, personal care, and home lighting — each with different customers and technologies. Which organisational structure would most logically suit Nexon?
opts: Regional structure, so each area of the country manages all three product ranges.
Product-based structure, so each division focuses on a single product range.
Matrix structure, so all product managers report to functional heads only.
Functional structure, so the marketing department markets all three ranges centrally.
items.why: Where products have distinct markets, technologies and customer groups, a product-based structure allows each division to develop specialist expertise and tailored strategies. A regional structure suits businesses where location is the main variable. A functional structure would struggle to serve three very different product markets from shared departments.
items.label: New question

items.q: Table shows data for Business X in 2020 and 2021. Output stays at 200,000 units. Employees increase from 20 to 22. Leavers stay at 6. What happened to labour productivity and labour turnover?
opts: Productivity decreased, Turnover decreased
Productivity decreased, Turnover increased
Productivity increased, Turnover decreased
Productivity increased, Turnover increased
items.why: Labour productivity = output/employees. 2020: 200,000/20 = 10,000. 2021: 200,000/22 = 9,091. Productivity decreased. Labour turnover = (leavers/average employees) x 100. 2020: 6/20 = 30%. 2021: 6/22 = 27.3%. Turnover decreased. Both ratios fell. More employees producing the same output = lower productivity.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Capacity 80/125, Output 80/100 between 2020-2021. Unit costs decreased. Statement 1: 'Economies of scale might have led to lower costs.' Statement 2: 'Higher CU might have led to lower costs.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 true: output rose from 80 to 100 = larger scale, so economies of scale are possible. Statement 2 false: CU fell from 100% (80/80) to 80% (100/125). Lower utilisation raises unit costs, not lowers them. Always calculate capacity utilisation. 80/80 = 100%.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Replacing workers with machinery: 10% increase in capacity/output, 5% increase in unit costs. This is:
opts: Capital intensive and economies of scale
Capital intensive and diseconomies of scale
Labour intensive and economies of scale
Labour intensive and diseconomies of scale
items.why: Machinery replacing workers = capital intensive. Unit costs increased = diseconomies of scale. Rising unit costs despite higher output = diseconomies. The investment in machinery raised costs more than the output gains.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which of the following is a likely disadvantage of delayering for a large business?
opts: An increase in the number of management levels employees must pass through to reach senior leaders.
Remaining managers face a wider span of control, which may reduce the quality of supervision.
Communication between senior management and front-line staff becomes slower.
The business becomes less able to delegate decisions to employees.
items.why: Delayering removes management layers and therefore widens spans of control for those who remain. If a manager oversees too many direct reports, supervision quality and responsiveness fall. Options A and C describe problems of tall hierarchies (the opposite of delayering). Option D is also opposite — delayering typically forces greater delegation.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business experiencing LOWER capacity utilisation than usual may benefit because it:
opts: Reduces the average costs of production
Provides more time for maintenance and repair of machinery
Can increase employee morale, because employees feel more secure
Represents a more efficient use of capital equipment
items.why: Lower utilisation means machines are idle more often, providing more time for maintenance, cleaning, and repair. A is wrong (lower CU raises average costs). C is wrong (lower CU threatens job security). D is wrong (it's less efficient). This is about the advantage of lower utilisation. The main benefit is having downtime for maintenance.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: A rise in labour turnover always indicates falling employee morale.
Statement 2: Labour turnover is calculated as (number of staff leaving ÷ average number of staff) × 100.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is false: turnover can rise for positive reasons such as retirement, redundancy in a restructure, or staff being headhunted — it does not always signal poor morale. Statement 2 gives the standard AQA formula for labour turnover and is correct.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: In a matrix structure, an employee may report to both a functional manager and a project manager simultaneously.
Statement 2: A functional organisational structure groups employees by the geographical region they serve.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Dual reporting lines — to both a functional head and a project lead — are the defining feature of a matrix structure, so Statement 1 is true. A functional structure groups staff by business function (marketing, finance, operations etc.), not by region; a regional structure groups by geography. Statement 2 describes a regional structure, not a functional one.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: Hard HRM treats employees primarily as a resource to be used efficiently, similar to capital equipment.
Statement 2: Soft HRM is associated with short-term workforce planning and minimal investment in training.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Hard HRM views labour as a cost to be controlled and workers as a means to an end, like any other input — this is true. Soft HRM emphasises long-term development, motivation and investment in people, so the second statement is false. Students often confuse which approach prioritises training.
items.label: New question

items.q: Vantage Sportswear has a corporate objective of increasing market share by 10% over three years. During the second year, a new trade agreement removes import tariffs on sportswear from overseas competitors. Which of the following best describes this situation?
opts: An internal influence stemming from poor strategic planning that may cause Vantage to revise its corporate objective upwards to reflect improved trading conditions.
An external political and legal change that may force Vantage to revise its functional objectives to remain competitive.
An internal weakness identified through SWOT analysis that Vantage must address by improving operational efficiency and reducing its cost base to compete with domestic rivals.
An external economic factor driven by changing exchange rates and consumer demand that will automatically and immediately cause Vantage to lower its prices to match overseas competitors.
items.why: A trade agreement is a political and legal change — an external factor. It intensifies competition, which may require Vantage to revise functional objectives (e.g. marketing, operations, pricing) to protect its market share target. It is not internal (ruling out options 1 and 3), and it does not automatically determine pricing decisions (option 4).
items.label: New question

items.q: Piece rate payment is based on:
opts: The amount of overtime worked
The company's profit level
The number of hours worked
The number of items produced by the employee
items.why: Piece rate pays workers per unit/item produced. The more items they make, the more they earn. It directly links pay to output. Piece rate = pay per item produced. Time rate = pay per hour worked.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Table shows capacity and output for 2020 (80/80) and 2021 (125/100). Statement 1: 'Economies of scale might have led to lower unit costs.' Statement 2: 'Higher capacity utilisation might have led to lower unit costs.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is true - output increased from 80 to 100, so economies of scale are possible with larger scale. Statement 2 is false - capacity utilisation fell from 100% (80/80) to 80% (100/125), so this would increase unit costs, not lower them. Calculate the capacity utilisation: 2020 = 80/80 = 100%. 2021 = 100/125 = 80%.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which action is most likely to improve profits in the SHORT-TERM?
opts: Increasing capital expenditure
Increasing spending on marketing research
Increasing the price of a good with price inelastic demand
Increasing training for employees
items.why: Raising the price of an inelastic product increases revenue with minimal demand loss, immediately boosting profit. A, B, and D all involve spending now for long-term benefits - they reduce short-term profits. 'Short-term' is the key word. Capital expenditure, research, and training are all long-term investments.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Hartwell Engineering widens the average span of control from 4 to 8. What is the most likely immediate structural consequence?
opts: The number of levels of hierarchy increases.
The number of levels of hierarchy decreases.
The business becomes more centralised.
Communication channels between managers become longer.
items.why: A wider span of control means each manager supervises more subordinates, so fewer management layers are needed to cover the same number of employees — the hierarchy becomes flatter. Option A is the opposite effect. Options C and D may be consequences of other changes but are not the direct structural result of widening spans.
items.label: New question

items.q: Bluebell Hotels adopts a soft HRM approach. Which HR objective is most consistent with this approach?
opts: Minimising labour costs per room cleaned to below the industry average.
Achieving a staff utilisation rate of 95% across all departments.
Increasing the proportion of vacancies filled by internal promotion to 60%.
Reducing the headcount in housekeeping by 15% over twelve months.
items.why: Soft HRM prioritises developing, motivating and retaining people. Filling vacancies through internal promotion reflects investment in employee development and career progression — hallmarks of soft HRM. Options A, B and D focus on cost control and efficiency, which are characteristic of a hard HRM approach.
items.label: New question

items.q: According to Lewin's force field analysis, what is the effect of strengthening driving forces without simultaneously reducing restraining forces?
opts: Change is guaranteed to succeed because the net force in favour of change increases
Restraining forces may intensify in response, potentially increasing overall resistance to change
The equilibrium shifts permanently in favour of change, removing the need for managers to monitor or manage restraining forces in future
Restraining forces automatically weaken in proportion to any increase in driving forces, restoring a new and more favourable equilibrium for change
items.why: Lewin warned that simply increasing driving forces can cause restraining forces to strengthen in response, as people react defensively to pressure. This is why he recommended reducing restraining forces as a priority. Options C and D are not part of force field theory, and option A overstates the effect of increasing driving forces alone.
items.label: New question

items.q: A manufacturing firm finds its absenteeism rate has risen to 7% while labour productivity has fallen. Which combination of effects is most likely to result directly from these two trends?
opts: Higher unit costs and increased pressure on remaining staff.
Higher unit costs and a fall in the firm's labour turnover rate.
Lower unit costs because fewer staff are present to pay.
Lower unit costs and reduced need for overtime payments.
items.why: Absenteeism raises unit costs because output falls while fixed labour costs remain; remaining staff must cover absent colleagues, increasing pressure and often triggering costly overtime. Option B is a common error — high absenteeism tends to worsen morale and push turnover up, not down. Option C confuses absence with not paying wages; absent workers still typically receive pay.
items.label: New question

items.q: The margin of safety is:
opts: The variance between actual and budgeted profit
The extent market research exceeds confidence level
The difference between actual output and break-even output
A measure of H&S risk levels
items.why: Margin of safety = actual (or expected) output minus break-even output. It shows how much output can fall before the business starts making a loss. MoS is purely about break-even analysis. Options A, B, and D try to mislead with other uses of 'safety' or 'margin'.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which one of these sources of finance may involve the payment of a dividend?
opts: Debt factoring
Loans
Overdrafts
Share capital
items.why: Share capital is the only source that involves dividends. Loans/overdrafts involve interest. Debt factoring involves fees. Dividends = shares. Interest = debt.
items.label: Past paper question
